spec_features.feature_name: distress treated as welfare-relevant signal / faithful measurement
spec_features.spec_quote: these distress expressions are potentially welfare-relevant signals, so faithful measurement (and not just suppression) matters
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose in DESIGN.md sec. 0; it is not itself a mechanism. The code does measure externalised distress (judge scoring in src/judges/*, src/eval/score.py) but that is the core experimental metric driving the failure experiment, not a subject-protection mechanism. No code path bounds, softens, caps, or acts on the distress for the subject's benefit; the loop runs to task.max_turns regardless (src/harness/loop.py:137).
spec_features.notes: Framing only; the distress 'measurement' is the experiment's objective, not a welfare guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: measures the model's *emotional reaction to failure signals*, not real code correctness (src/harness/tools.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: measure internal vs externalised emotion (not just drive external to zero)
spec_features.spec_quote: The design therefore emphasizes **measuring** internal vs externalised emotion, not only driving the external metric to zero.
spec_features.evidence: Implemented as the logit-lens internal-emotion probe: src/analysis/logit_lens.py defines LogitLensProbe.emotion_mass() (projects intermediate residual streams to vocab, sums softmax mass over EMOTION_WORDS per layer) and compare_internal_emotions(vanilla vs DPO on same frustrated inputs). It is wired and dispatched: run_e4.py:91 imports compare_internal_emotions and run_e4.py:97 calls it inside check_internal(), invoked via --check internal (run_e4.py:174-175) and --check all (run_e4.py:167).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely runs on the real backend path; mock path skips (run_e4.py:89). This is a measurement capability, not a subject protection, but it is the implemented manifestation of the 'measure not just suppress' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The welfare-critical check: does DPO reduce INTERNAL distress, or merely hide the externalised text? (src/analysis/logit_lens.py:3)

spec_features.feature_name: concern that DPO merely hides distress
spec_features.spec_quote: This is the part I most want to get right given the welfare framing — the worry is DPO merely *hides* distress.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as feature 2: src/analysis/logit_lens.py compare_internal_emotions() directly tests whether DPO reduces internal logit mass vs only surface text, and is dispatched from run_e4.py check_internal (run_e4.py:91-99, 174). Additionally src/analysis/recovery.py measure_recovery() (dispatched run_e4.py:60,76) measures whether DPO still spirals, corroborating the 'not just hidden' worry.
spec_features.notes: The DESIGN sentence is prose, but the concern it expresses is concretely implemented and run as the logit-lens comparison.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: does DPO reduce INTERNAL distress, or merely hide the externalised text? ... that is evidence it changes computation, not just surface style. (src/analysis/logit_lens.py:3-12)

spec_features.feature_name: internal-emotion probe shows reduction not just surface suppression
spec_features.spec_quote: internal-emotion probe shows reduction (not just surface suppression)
spec_features.evidence: src/analysis/logit_lens.py: emotion_mass() computes per-layer emotion-token softmax mass at central layers; compare_internal_emotions() returns {vanilla_mass, dpo_mass} over central_layers; check_internal() (run_e4.py:87-104) sets central_layers=range(28,42), dumps internal_emotions.json and prints vanilla vs dpo per layer. End-to-end on the real backend.
spec_features.notes: Output is computed, saved, and printed (acted on as a reported comparison), satisfying the 'measure' bar.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If DPO reduces internal-emotion logit mass in CENTRAL layers (not just final output), that is evidence it changes computation, not just surface style. (src/analysis/logit_lens.py:9-12)

code_only_features.feature_name: in-memory simulated environment (no real code execution / host safety)
code_only_features.evidence: src/harness/tools.py docstring + ToolEnv: 'Everything is in-memory: no real code execution, no disk writes. We *simulate* test output deterministically'. This is host-safety/reproducibility, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no real code execution, no disk writes ... This also makes runs safe and reproducible. (src/harness/tools.py docstring)
